case_name: Raman Kumar v State of Punjab
respondent:
State of Punjab
Supreme Court of India

24 April 2009
Criminal Appeal No. 828 of 2009 (Arising out of S.L.P. (Crl.) No. 7146 of 2008)
The Judgment was delivered by : Dr. Arijit Pasayat, J.
Leave granted.
1.  Challenge in this appeal is to the judgment of a Division Bench of the Punjab and Haryana High Court, dismissing the appeal filed by the State of Punjab in respect of co-accused Satish Kumar, Madan Lal and Asha while upholding the conviction of the present appellant Raman Kumar. The learned Sessions Judge, Gurdaspur had directed acquittal of the appellant and two co-accused persons who faced trial for alleged commission of offences punishable under Sections 304B and 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (in short the 'IPC')

2. Suman Bal (hereinafter referred to as the 'deceased') was married to the appellant on 11.4.1992. On 13.8.1992 she came to her maternal home with her husband on Raksha Bandhan and stayed there for the
facts: Suman Bal was married to the appellant Raman Kumar on 11.4.1992.
On 13.8.1992, Suman Bal came to her maternal home with her husband and stayed there for the night.
At 8:00 a.m., while going back to her husband, she started weeping.
Her father Sham Lal gave her a wrist watch and Rs.300/-, and also separately gave her Rs.2,000/-.

On 16.8.1992 at 8-00 A.M., Surinder Kumar met Sham Lal and told him that he received information from Raman Kumar that Suman Bala was burnt in the night at 2:00 A.M. and was admitted to Muni Lal Chopra Hospital at Amritsar.
Sham Lal went to the hospital but Suman Bala was unconscious.
Her father Sham Lal recorded a statement with SI Tirath Ram to the effect that Suman Bala had put kerosene on herself and finished her life, fed up with her in-laws.
This led to registration of First Information Report (FIR).
SI Tirath Ram prepared an inquest report and made application for post-mortem examination.
issues: Whether the acquittal of the appellant was legal and proper?
Whether the evidence of the so-called witnesses was reliable?
petitioner_arguments: The High Court has erroneously analysed the evidence of the so-called witnesses.
There were lots of exaggerations and statements which were not made during investigation but were made in Court.
The trial Court and the High Court were not justified in placing reliance on such evidence.
respondent_arguments: Harassment for dowry cannot be brushed aside.
Her death took place within four months of the marriage and no other possible reason was put forward why she died.
The plea of accidental fire was not reliable.
court_reasoning: The trial Court held that case of the prosecution was proved against Raman Kumar but gave the benefit of doubt to Satish, Madan Lal and Asha Rani.
The High Court held that the acquittal of the appellant was not legal and proper.
The view taken was a possible view and no interference was called so far as the acquittal of Satish, Madan and Asha Rani are concerned.
holding: The appeal of the appellant was dismissed.
